text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

Abstract
We assessed whether GEO accessions GSE309890 and GDS309890 represent the same record. We used the NCBI GEO accession resolver to deterministically map each accession to its internal Entrez UID, record type, and canonical URLs. The query resolved both accessions (2 requested, 2 resolved). GSE309890 maps to a GEO Series (entry_type: GSE) with UID 200309890 and an FTP directory under geo/series. GDS309890 maps to a curated GEO DataSet (entry_type: GDS) with UID 309890 and an FTP directory under geo/datasets. These differences indicate they are distinct record types with separate identifiers and storage locations. Clarifying accession equivalence is important for reproducible data retrieval and correct tool selection: Series (GSE) organize experiments and samples, while curated DataSets (GDS) are NCBI-curated derivations available for a subset of studies. Our result provides unambiguous provenance and URLs to guide subsequent retrieval.

I. Introduction
Background. The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) uses accession prefixes to denote different record types. GEO Series (GSE) aggregate samples and experimental design, while curated DataSets (GDS) are curated, standardized datasets produced for selected studies. Determining whether similarly numbered GSE and GDS accessions refer to the same entity is a common practical question in data reuse.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. Whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 are the same record, or distinct types related to one study, was unresolved.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Resolve both accessions to confirm their record types, identifiers, and URLs. Hypothesis: GSE309890 and GDS309890 are different record types with distinct UIDs and directories, and are not the same record.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We used a GEO-specific resolver that maps GEO accessions to Entrez UIDs and canonical URLs. This approach avoids ambiguity from free-text searches and returns type-checked identifiers.
Materials.
- NCBI GEO; tool: geo_resolve_accession.
Procedures.
- functions.geo_resolve_accession with arguments: accessions="GSE309890 GDS309890".
- Default behavior: return UID, entry_type, FTP directory URL, and GEO page URL for each accession.
Statistical Analysis. We reported the counts directly from the resolver: requested (2) and resolved (2). No deduplication was necessary. Differences were assessed by exact string comparison of entry_type, UID, ftp_directory_url, and geo_url fields.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Resolution of GEO accessions and canonical URLs

| Accession   | Entry Type | UID       | FTP Directory URL                                                      | GEO Page URL                                                     |
|-------------|------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890   | GSE        | 200309890 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/          | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890    |
| GDS309890   | GDS        | 309890    | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/        | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890    |

Findings. Two accessions were requested and two were resolved. GSE309890 is a GEO Series with UID 200309890. GDS309890 is a curated GEO DataSet with UID 309890. The FTP directories and GEO page URLs differ in path and prefix.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not the same record. They are distinct GEO record types with separate UIDs and storage locations. The resolver’s rule confirms UID formatting differences by type, supporting this distinction.
Context. The returned entry_type values (GSE vs. GDS) and directory paths (geo/series vs. geo/datasets) are consistent with GEO’s data organization and indicate different roles: Series organize study-level content, curated DataSets provide standardized results for selected studies.
Limitations. The resolver confirms identity and canonical URLs but does not assert whether a specific GDS is curated from a specific GSE. Establishing such a relationship would require fetching and comparing record metadata or links.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 and GDS309890 are distinct GEO records. A next step is to retrieve both records (e.g., via GEO Series and GDS detail queries) to determine whether GDS309890 curates data from GSE309890 and to locate processed files of interest.

References
[1] NCBI GEO: GSE309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO: GDS309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890
[3] NCBI GEO FTP (GSE309890). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[4] NCBI GEO FTP (GDS309890). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/

Acknowledgments
We acknowledge NCBI GEO for accession resolution and record hosting.
